\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{മേലുദ്യോഗസ്ഥൻ} (mēludyōgasthan)}{മേലുദ്യോഗസ്ഥൻ (mēludyōgasthan)}]{\ml{മേലുദ്യോഗസ്ഥൻ} (mēludyōgasthan) — a superior; a senior officer}

\label{lesson:ML-C545-meludyogasthan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a work shift, then the Malayalam for to be interrupted.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{മേലുദ്യോഗസ്ഥൻ}}
\textbf{\ml{മേലുദ്യോഗസ്ഥൻ}} — \emph{mēludyōgasthan} — \textquotedblleft{}a superior; a senior officer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{മേലുദ്യോഗസ്ഥൻ} \ml{എന്റെ} \ml{റിപ്പോർട്ട്} \ml{പരിശോധിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mēludyōgasthan enṟe ṟippōrṭṭŭ pariśōdhiccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My superior checked my report.
\end{quote}

\ml{മേൽ} above + \ml{ഉദ്യോഗസ്ഥൻ} an official.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{മേലുദ്യോഗസ്ഥൻ}} (\emph{mēludyōgasthan}) is a Malayalam compound built from \ml{മേൽ}, \textquotedblleft{}above\textquotedblright{}, which is native (DEDR 5086), and \ml{ഉദ്യോഗസ്ഥൻ}, \textquotedblleft{}an official\textquotedblright{}, from Sanskrit \emph{udyoga} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mēludyōgasthan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mēludyōgasthan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mēludyōgasthan enṟe ṟippōrṭṭŭ pariśōdhiccu.} — My superior checked my report.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a work shift, then the Malayalam for to be interrupted, then say \emph{mēludyōgasthan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{മേലുദ്യോഗസ്ഥൻ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A superior; a senior officer\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ചുമതല} (cumatala)}{ചുമതല (cumatala)}]{\ml{ചുമതല} (cumatala) — being in charge; a duty}

\label{lesson:ML-C545-cumatala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to be interrupted, then the Malayalam for a superior.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ചുമതല}}
\textbf{\ml{ചുമതല}} — \emph{cumatala} — \textquotedblleft{}being in charge; a duty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ഓഫീസിലെ} \ml{പുതിയ} \ml{പദ്ധതിയുടെ} \ml{ചുമതല} \ml{എനിക്കാണ്}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ōphīsile putiya paddhatiyuṭe cumatala enikkāṇŭ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I am in charge of the office's new project.
\end{quote}

\ml{ചുമതല} \ml{ഏൽക്കുക}, to take charge.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ചുമതല}} (\emph{cumatala}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 2677 lists it beside \ml{ചുമ}, \textquotedblleft{}a load\textquotedblright{}, and \ml{ചുമക്കുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to carry\textquotedblright{}: a duty is a load one carries (DEDR 2677).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cumatala}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cumatala}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ōphīsile putiya paddhatiyuṭe cumatala enikkāṇŭ.} — I am in charge of the office's new project.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to be interrupted, then the Malayalam for a superior, then say \emph{cumatala} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ചുമതല} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Being in charge; a duty\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{സ്ഥലംമാറ്റം} (sthalaṁmāṟṟaṁ)}{സ്ഥലംമാറ്റം (sthalaṁmāṟṟaṁ)}]{\ml{സ്ഥലംമാറ്റം} (sthalaṁmāṟṟaṁ) — a job transfer}

\label{lesson:ML-C545-sthalammarram}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a superior, then the Malayalam for being in charge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{സ്ഥലംമാറ്റം}}
\textbf{\ml{സ്ഥലംമാറ്റം}} — \emph{sthalaṁmāṟṟaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}a job transfer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{അച്ഛന്} \ml{വടക്കൻ} \ml{ജില്ലയിലേക്ക്} \ml{സ്ഥലംമാറ്റം} \ml{കിട്ടി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{acchanŭ vaṭakkan jillayilēkkŭ sthalaṁmāṟṟaṁ kiṭṭi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Father got a transfer to a northern district.
\end{quote}

\ml{സ്ഥലം} a place + \ml{മാറ്റം} a change; common for government staff.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{സ്ഥലംമാറ്റം}} (\emph{sthalaṁmāṟṟaṁ}) is a Malayalam compound built from \ml{സ്ഥലം}, from Sanskrit \emph{sthala}, \textquotedblleft{}ground, a place\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13744), and \ml{മാറ്റം}, \textquotedblleft{}a change\textquotedblright{}, which is native (DEDR 4834).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sthalaṁmāṟṟaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sthalaṁmāṟṟaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{acchanŭ vaṭakkan jillayilēkkŭ sthalaṁmāṟṟaṁ kiṭṭi.} — Father got a transfer to a northern district.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a superior, then the Malayalam for being in charge, then say \emph{sthalaṁmāṟṟaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ആസൂത്രണം} (āsūtraṇaṁ)}{ആസൂത്രണം (āsūtraṇaṁ)}]{\ml{ആസൂത്രണം} (āsūtraṇaṁ) — planning}

\label{lesson:ML-C545-asutranam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for being in charge, then the Malayalam for a job transfer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ആസൂത്രണം}}
\textbf{\ml{ആസൂത്രണം}} — \emph{āsūtraṇaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}planning\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{നല്ല} \ml{ആസൂത്രണം} \ml{ഉണ്ടെങ്കിൽ} \ml{ജോലി} \ml{എളുപ്പമാകും}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nalla āsūtraṇaṁ uṇṭeṅkil jōli eḷuppamākuṁ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
With good planning the work becomes easy.
\end{quote}

\ml{ആസൂത്രണം} \ml{ചെയ്യുക} is to plan.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ആസൂത്രണം}} (\emph{āsūtraṇaṁ}) is a learned word built on Sanskrit \emph{sūtra}, \textquotedblleft{}a thread, a cord\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13561); the exact model of the formation is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āsūtraṇaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āsūtraṇaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nalla āsūtraṇaṁ uṇṭeṅkil jōli eḷuppamākuṁ.} — With good planning the work becomes easy.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for being in charge, then the Malayalam for a job transfer, then say \emph{āsūtraṇaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ആസൂത്രണം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Planning\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{സഹകരിക്കുക} (sahakarikkuka)}{സഹകരിക്കുക (sahakarikkuka)}]{\ml{സഹകരിക്കുക} (sahakarikkuka) — to cooperate}

\label{lesson:ML-C545-sahakarikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a job transfer, then the Malayalam for planning.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{സഹകരിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{സഹകരിക്കുക}} — \emph{sahakarikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to cooperate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{എല്ലാവരും} \ml{സഹകരിച്ചതുകൊണ്ട്} \ml{പരിപാടി} \ml{വിജയിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ellāvaruṁ sahakariccatukoṇṭŭ paripāṭi vijayiccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The programme succeeded because everyone cooperated.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{സഹകരിച്ചു}, \emph{sahakariccu}.

The noun is \ml{സഹകരണം}, cooperation; the partner takes -\ml{ഓട്}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{സഹകരിക്കുക}} (\emph{sahakarikkuka}) is built from Sanskrit \emph{sahakāra}, \textquotedblleft{}assistance\textquotedblright{}, \emph{saha} \textquotedblleft{}with\textquotedblright{} and \emph{kāra} \textquotedblleft{}doing\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13299), with the Malayalam verb ending -\ml{ിക്കുക}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sahakarikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ellāvaruṁ sahakariccatukoṇṭŭ paripāṭi vijayiccu.} — The programme succeeded because everyone cooperated.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a job transfer, then the Malayalam for planning, then say \emph{sahakarikkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
